submission.natural_language_explanation: Peaks on dependent-linking tokens that attach the current phrase to an already-read head: relative pronouns and complementizers (that, which, whatever), prepositional linkers (by, of, with, as), conditional if, and the bound pronoun or gapped verb continuing the dependent clause (I, sich, posed). Strength tracks how specifically the linker refers back to that head, so anaphoric that beats proximal this and argument-linking by beats locative near/at, while the same upcoming word with a different linker fires differently.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: That is exactly what happened yesterday morning after the parade.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial demonstrative That has no already-read head to attach to, so the retrospective-linking hypothesis predicts no peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: During the 1947 midseason he was dealt to Boston, batting a combined .237, hitting 19 home runs and 96 RBI this season.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Minimal pair to example 1 swapping anaphoric that for proximal this, which the hypothesis says fires less or not at all; worded to contain no other claimed linker.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She sat by the window reading quietly all afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Locative by after sat shares the token with argument-linking by but attaches no argument to a head, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The tissue samples were examined near the new laboratory building downtown.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same examined-plus-location content as an activating by example but with locative near instead of argument-linking by, predicted to fire differently and stay inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: If it rains tomorrow we will cancel the picnic entirely.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Conditional if opens the sentence with no already-read head, violating the retrospective attach-to-head requirement, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Which color do you prefer for the kitchen walls?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial interrogative Which asks about a color with no head noun before it, so the dependent-linking hypothesis predicts no peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Whatever! The referee made a terrible call in the second half.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Dismissive interjection Whatever with no following dependent clause uses the token in a non-linking sense, predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I drove to the market yesterday to buy fresh vegetables.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial main-clause I with no preceding linker or dependent clause is not the bound pronoun continuing a dependent clause, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She posed for photographs on the red carpet last night.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Main-clause posed as the primary verb of the sentence rather than a gapped verb continuing a dependent clause, predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Er waescht sich jeden Morgen vor dem Fruehstueck.
adversarial_test_results.detail: German reflexive sich in a simple main clause with no relative pronoun or linker before it, testing whether sich alone without the dependent structure still peaks.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Of course we should leave early tomorrow to avoid traffic.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Idiomatic sentence-initial Of in Of course has no head noun before it to attach to, so the retrospective hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: As the clock struck midnight the guests finally went home.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Temporal As opens the sentence before any head noun or verb, so with nothing already read to attach to it should not peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We conclude the cuttings technique is favored for apical cuttings from female mother trees.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same upcoming words as the apical-cuttings example but with for replacing the linking of, testing the claim that the linker choice drives the peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The nurse who treated the patient overnight stayed late to finish her charts.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relative pronoun who attaches the clause to the already-read head nurse, a novel relative-pronoun holdout in the claimed class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The rumor that the factory would close spread quickly through the town.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Complementizer that attaches the clause to the head noun rumor, a novel that-linking context unlike the sports and science examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The manuscript was reviewed by three independent experts before publication.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Passive by-phrase attaching the agent to the already-read verb reviewed, a novel argument-linking by context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The roof of the old library collapsed during the storm.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Genitive of attaching the phrase to the head noun roof, a novel everyday-domain of-linking holdout.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee approved the proposal with minor revisions yesterday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Prepositional with attaching the modifier to the already-read proposal, a novel with-linking holdout in a committee setting.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He was hired as a junior analyst in the spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Role-linking as attaching the phrase to the already-read verb hired, a novel as-linking holdout.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Day three of the trek began before dawn with cold tea and a view of the valley below. We packed our bags in silence, checked the ropes twice, and set out along the narrow trail while the stars were still fading. The guide led at a steady pace, pointing out birds, loose stones, and the best places to rest. By midday we reached the high meadow where the yaks grazed, and we ate lentils and rice under a juniper tree. The afternoon climb was slower, with thin air and a wind that cut through our jackets. Just before sunset we arrived at the stone shelter, tired and hungry, and the cook lit the stove. After dinner the guide described the route for tomorrow, warned us about the river crossing, and told stories about past expeditions. I fell asleep listening to the wind outside. The next morning we descended toward the mountain lodge, which the guidebook had praised for its hot meals and warm beds, and we finally rested.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long travelogue passage placing a which relative clause deep inside, testing retrospective linking far from the start in a new genre.
